subject: Control plane assertion routing and SCIM provisioning compatibility review
messages:
From: Karen Liu <karen.liu@nbank.com>

Cc: infra-team@nordicbank.com
Date: Wed, 21 May 2025 16:12:00 +0200
Subject: Private CP SAML routing question + SCIM provisioning caveats

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We ran a short spike against the on-prem control plane shim and hit two items that I want to surface before we proceed with the full cutover: 

1) Assertion routing: when the control plane endpoint is in our VPC and requests are routed through the IDP proxy, the SAML assertion contains an "audience" that points to the public control-plane hostname. Will your private control plane accept an audience that resolves to an internal ELB hostname (nb-cp-priv-elb.internal)? Our security team is worried about mismatches causing auth failures.

2) SCIM provisioning: our provisioning flows create service accounts with delegated roles. We saw a 409 when SCIM attempted to PATCH a role mapping that already exists with a slightly different case in the externalId. Is SCIM idempotent in the private control plane, or should we add normalization on our side?

Can you confirm expected behavior and any known workarounds? Also attaching a small sample of the SAML assertion (redacted) and the SCIM patch payload we used.

Best,
Karen Liu
Engineering Manager, Identity Platform
NordicBank

Subject: Re: Private CP SAML routing question + SCIM provisioning caveats

Hi Karen — thanks for the clear repro notes and the samples. Looping in Ben (runtime/authz), Karthik (onboarding/SCIM) and Jordan (network/security) so we can give authoritative answers.

Short answers up front:
- Assertion audience: private control plane accepts an audience that matches the TLS SNI presented at the gateway. It does not require the public hostname specifically; we validate the SAML "AudienceRestriction" against the cert name presented by the customer-side ELB/proxy. That said, a mismatch between the Audience value and the SNI will be rejected.
- SCIM idempotency: the SCIM service in private control plane normalizes resource externalIds to NFC Unicode and lowercases attribute keys for matching, but it preserves case for display names. The 409 you saw is likely from a backend index (we have strict unique-index semantics for externalId) — we can provide a reconciliation patch that performs a case-insensitive merge during onboarding.

Proposed next steps:
1) We will run a targeted validation: have NordicBank temporarily set the SAML Audience to the internal ELB name (nb-cp-priv-elb.internal) and present the same client cert/SNI from your proxy so we can reproduce.
2) Ben will prepare a compact assertion-routing matrix and a recommended mapping for OIDC/SAML audience -> control-plane-trust anchor.
3) Karthik will prepare a SCIM reconciliation patch and a runbook with idempotent examples (PATCH vs PUT, idempotency keys).
4) Schedule a 60-minute joint test window; Jordan and Karen to agree on network egress rules for the test.

I attached a short matrix and a sample SCIM merge patch we can try. If this looks good, we'll schedule the test for tomorrow morning your time.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- controlplane-assertion-routing-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)
- scim-provisioning-sample.patch (patch)

On Wed, May 21, 2025 at 05:03 PM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
> Short answers up front:
> - Assertion audience: private control plane accepts an audience that matches the TLS SNI presented at the gateway. It does not require the public hostname specifically; we validate the SAML "AudienceRestriction" against the cert name presented by the customer-side ELB/proxy.

A couple implementation notes / gotchas from the runtime side:
- If the incoming request traverses a TLS-terminating reverse proxy that rewrites Host headers (common in some F5 configurations), our gateway will validate against the SNI, not the Host header. So customers must ensure SNI matches the Audience in their assertion.
- For hybrid setups (control plane endpoint accessible both publicly and via internal DNS), we recommend canonicalizing the audience at the IDP to the internal name used by your LB (nb-cp-priv-elb.internal) and publishing that name in your DNS with an internal A record that matches the LB. This avoids split-brain assertion issues.
- For the 409 SCIM case: our index checks include a trimmed-string equality. Common causes: trailing unicode whitespace or invisible unicode characters. The reconciliation patch Karthik is preparing should tolerate these and re-index if you opt-in.

I'll be available during the test window — my ask is that you snapshot logs (authn/audit) and share the trace IDs so we can correlate to our gateway.

-ben

All — following up with the SCIM patch and timing. Summary of what I'll run during the validation window: 

- Normalize incoming externalId by trimming, Unicode NFC normalization, and lowercasing for matching.
- If a conflict (409) is detected, the patch will attempt a safe-merge: create an alias mapping from the conflicting externalId -> canonical externalId and then complete the patch. This leaves both identifiers discoverable via a quick lookup endpoint.
- I'll also enable a verbose reconciliation mode for the onboarding run (30-minute window) that emits a reconciliation report to the shared Drive link.

Proposed test window: Fri 2025-05-23 09:00-10:00 CET. Jordan: can you confirm network egress rules and whether the internal ELB will preserve SNI when proxied through your gateway? Karen: can you set up a test assertion with audience=nb-cp-priv-elb.internal and share the sample assertion before the window?

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Onboarding
Redwood Inference
